title: improve
text:
Ramabana loads a learned folder into every session: AGENTS.md, a few short rules included in every briefing, and skills it opens when a task calls for them. A round tries to improve that folder from one finished session, in the manner of the propose, probe and compose step of Harness². It replays the session’s request k times from the commit the session started at, under the current folder. An editor model reads those runs and edits a copy of the folder. The request is replayed once more under the copy. The copy is kept only when that run replied, took a cheaper route than every base run, and a judge model rated its reply at least as good as the best base reply. A kept lesson becomes an entry in the day’s learning file, committed on a pending/ branch of the folder’s own git repository, one branch per round.

title: improve
text:
Runs
replay_clone makes a throwaway clone of the repository at the commit a session started from. The clone shares no object files with the source and has no remote, so a replay can neither change nor push to the original. run_turn runs one Ramabana turn with no interface, in a fresh config folder, so no history, extension, skill or project note from the person’s own config takes part. It reads the turn back from that folder’s history, which records the request, every tool call and the reply, and leaves Ramabana’s output in run.log. Writes are refused unless approve allows them. A round’s replays pass read_outside, so they can read installed packages and other folders the way an interactive session does, while their writes stay inside their clone.

title: improve
text:
Comparing runs
A route’s cost is a tuple of its route findings, its failed calls and its calls, and a smaller tuple is a cheaper route. A replay has nobody to answer approvals, so a refused approval does not count as a failure and asking again does not count as a denial_retry; in a real session a person would have answered. delivered says whether a run produced an answer at all: at least one model turn, a reply, no error, and a state of complete. A run that was stopped, abandoned or interrupted has no error, but its reply is cut short. better passes a candidate only when it delivered and costs less than every base run. Tying the best base run is not enough.
A cheaper route alone proves little, because an agent that gives up early is cheap too. So a round then asks a judge model, through judge_reply, to compare every reply, unlabelled and shuffled, and keeps the candidate only when the judge answers YES: its reply is at least as complete and correct as the best base reply. The judge also sees the shell commands each run asked for and was refused, and, when the round has it, what the person’s own session ran. A run that proposed the command the work needed is then not marked down for having been refused.

test_eq(route_cost(turn(shell_grep)), (1, 0, 1))     # a shell grep is a bypass finding
unasked = dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'pytest -q'}, detail='Denied by human operator. Reason given: nothing is listening for approvals')
test_eq(route_cost(turn(ls) | {'activity': [dict(tool='ls', ok=True, args={'path': ''}), unasked]}), (0, 0, 2))   # a replay's unanswered approval is not the agent's failure
test_eq(route_cost(turn(ls) | {'activity': [unasked, unasked]}), (0, 0, 2))   # nor is asking again
assert better(turn(ls), [base, turn(ls, ls2)])
assert not better(turn(ls, ls2), [base, turn(ls, ls2)]) # ties the best base run
assert not better(turn(ls, reply=''), [base])
assert not better(turn(reply='claude/sonnet failed (ClaudeError)') | {'usage': {'turns': 0}}, [base])   # no model turn ran: the reply is the failure
assert delivered(turn(ls) | {'usage': '{"turns": 2}'}) and delivered(turn(ls) | {'usage': None})
assert delivered(turn(ls) | {'state': 'complete'}) and not better(turn(ls) | {'state': 'abandoned'}, [base])
for st in ('cancelled', 'abandoned', 'interrupted'): assert not delivered(turn(ls) | {'state': st}), st   # a run cut off, with no error

title: improve
text:
The learned folder
A candidate folder may hold AGENTS.md, skills at skills/<name>/SKILL.md whose frontmatter gives the skill’s name and a description, and Dhrona’s dated learning files. check_learned lists anything else as a problem, and a round does not run a candidate that has one. AGENTS.md may hold LEARNED_MAX characters (2,000). The dated files are outside that limit. Hidden entries, such as .git and the .kosha index Ramabana writes into any folder it opens, are not part of the folder.
keep_lesson keeps what a round learned as an entry in dhrona-<date>.md, one file a day. An entry holds the request as a heading and the round’s notes, and no diff. keep_lesson commits the file on a new pending/<id> branch, so a person reviews it before it reaches HEAD. It does not check the branch out and does not touch the folder’s branch, index or files, so a person’s uncommitted edit stays as it was. A batch, a keep and a compaction run whatever the person has left uncommitted. committed_copy gives each replay the folder’s HEAD, so a replay never sees uncommitted text.
The dated files have their own limit, DATED_MAX (4,000 characters across all of them). A keep that would pass it raises ValueError, and the round reports the reason in problems. Ramabana loads dated files newest first within its own budget, so the limit only stops unbounded growth. A dated file whose date is over DATED_DAYS (30) days old is removed by expire_dated.
keep commits a candidate on a new pending/<id> branch of the folder’s own repository, as Dhrona, and leaves the folder’s files alone. keep_lesson and a compaction use it, and a person accepts the branch with ramabana-learned accept <id>. learned_repo makes the folder a repository the first time and commits what it already held. In an existing repository it leaves uncommitted changes alone.
Personal details never reach the learned folder or the editor and judge. scrub masks emails, phone numbers, keys and other identifying values with rahasya, as numbered labels such as [EMAIL_1]. It runs over every evidence file, the judge’s prompt, the editor’s notes and commit message, and every file of a candidate before the candidate is run, so what is tested is what is kept.

    (cand/'notes.txt').write_text('x')

    test_eq(len(check_learned(cand)), 2)

    assert b.startswith(PENDING)
    test_eq(sorted(_files(learned)), ['skills/stale/SKILL.md'])   # the working tree, which Ramabana reads, is untouched
    git = lambda *a: _git(learned, *a)
    assert 'skills/stale/SKILL.md' in git('show', '--stat', 'HEAD')   # what was there before Dhrona is the first commit
    test_eq(git('ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', b).split(), ['AGENTS.md', 'skills/sizes/SKILL.md'])
    test_eq(git('log', '-1', '--format=%an %s', b), 'Dhrona Read sizes from ls; ask [EMAIL_1]')
    test_eq(len(git('worktree', 'list').splitlines()), 1)   # the worktree it committed in is gone
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit')
    assert keep(cand, learned, 'again') != b   # a hand edit does not stop a keep, and the keep leaves it alone
    test_eq((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'a hand edit')
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').unlink()
    assert not _uncommitted(learned_repo(d/'empty')) and _git(d/'empty', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')   # an empty folder gets an empty first commit
    (cand/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Mail ann@example.com or call +1 415 555 0134.\n')
    test_eq(_scrub_folder(cand), ['AGENTS.md'])
    test_eq((cand/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'Mail [EMAIL_1] or call [PHONE_1].\n')

Ramabana writes a .kosha code index into every folder it opens, so one can sit untracked in the learned folder. Untracked hidden paths are not a person’s edit, as _files and keep already treat them, and learned_repo keeps .kosha/ out of a new repository’s status. A modified AGENTS.md does not block a batch, a keep or a compaction: Dhrona never stages, commits or discards a person’s edit.

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read sizes from `ls`.\n')
    learned_repo(learned)
    (learned/'.kosha').mkdir(); (learned/'.kosha'/'code.db').write_bytes(b'\x95\x00')
    assert '.kosha/' in (learned/'.git'/'info'/'exclude').read_text()
    (learned/'.git'/'info'/'exclude').write_text('')   # a repository made before the exclude line existed
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain'), '?? .kosha/')
    test_eq(_uncommitted(learned), False)
    test_eq(learned_repo(learned), learned)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit')
    test_eq(_uncommitted(learned), True)
    test_eq(learned_repo(learned), learned)   # an edit is not a reason to refuse
    status = _git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain')
status

A kept lesson is a short entry in dhrona-<date>.md: the request as a heading and the round’s notes under it, with no diff of the files the editor changed. keep_lesson commits that file on a new pending/<id> branch off HEAD, in a temporary worktree. It does not check the branch out, and it does not touch the learned folder’s checked-out branch, index or files, so a person’s uncommitted edit stays as it was. A second lesson on the same day goes on its own branch off the same HEAD. Its file holds both entries, because it starts from the first branch’s file.

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read sizes from `ls`.\n')
    learned_repo(learned)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit\n')   # a person's uncommitted edit
    (learned/'notes.txt').write_text('draft'); _git(learned, 'add', 'notes.txt')   # and a staged file
    state = lambda: (_git(learned, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'), _git(learned, 'branch', '--show-current'), _git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain'),
                     (learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), sorted(_files(learned)))
    before = state()
    entry = lesson_entry('sizes of the big files', 'Read file sizes with `ls`. Ask ann@example.com.')
    b = keep_lesson(learned, entry, 'Lesson from a replay: sizes of the big files')
    assert b.startswith(PENDING)
    test_eq(state(), before)   # branch, index, working tree and HEAD are as they were
    name = f'dhrona-{datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}.md'
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'diff', '--name-only', 'HEAD', b), name)
    text = _git(learned, 'show', f'{b}:{name}')
    assert 'Read file sizes with `ls`' in text and '[EMAIL_1]' in text and not any(m in text for m in ('@@', '+++', '```diff'))
    b2 = keep_lesson(learned, lesson_entry('a second request', 'Use `ls -l`.'), 'Lesson from a replay: a second request')
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'rev-parse', f'{b2}^'), _git(learned, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'))
    test_eq(len(_git(learned, 'worktree', 'list').splitlines()), 1)   # no worktree is left behind
    test_eq(state(), before)
    both = _git(learned, 'show', f'{b2}:{name}')
test_eq(both.count('\n## '), 2)
print(both)

LEARNED_MAX (2,000 characters) counts AGENTS.md alone. Dated learning files have their own cap, DATED_MAX (4,000 characters across all of them). keep_lesson raises ValueError for a lesson that would take the dated files past it, and a round reports that reason in problems. Ramabana loads dated files newest first within its own budget, so the cap only stops unbounded growth.

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('x' * LEARNED_MAX)
    (learned/'dhrona-2026-01-01.md').write_text('y' * (DATED_MAX - 100))
    test_eq(check_learned(learned), [])   # dated files are outside `LEARNED_MAX`
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('x' * (LEARNED_MAX + 1))
    test_eq(len(check_learned(learned)), 1)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('x' * LEARNED_MAX)
    learned_repo(learned)
    test_fail(lambda: keep_lesson(learned, 'z' * 200, 'Lesson from a replay: long'), contains=f'{DATED_MAX:,}')
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'branch', '--list', 'pending/*'), '')   # a refused lesson leaves no branch
    b = keep_lesson(learned, lesson_entry('short', 'z' * 20), 'Lesson from a replay: short')
    files = _git(learned, 'ls-tree', '--name-only', b)
files

Evidence for the editor
The editor model reads files, not one long prompt. trajectory_md writes one turn as markdown: the request, each tool call with its arguments, outcome and shortened result, and the reply. findings_md lists each run’s route cost, its findings and its failed or refused calls.     cfg:str='~/.config/ramabana', days:int=30, now:NoneType=None
):
Lessons remember recorded in Ramabana’s history in the last days days, newest first, one per lesson text, scrubbed.


recent_lessons reads the lessons the agent recorded with remember from Ramabana’s history. Every remember call is in the history whether the session had a vault or only a memory file, and shalya’s parse_lesson reads the fields back the same way for both. Only structured lessons count, one per lesson text, newest first, from the last days days, with personal details scrubbed. lessons_md writes them for the editor as lessons.md, tool defects first, because a tool defect is a candidate for a skill that works around it.

    rows = [dict(session='s1', at=time.time() - 40*86400, activity=[rem(text='old lesson', cue='c', component='rule')]),

    got = recent_lessons(cfg)
    test_eq([(l['lesson'], l['session']) for l in got], [('Filter on the root-relative path', 's3')])   # newest wins; old, plain, invalid and refused are left out
    got = recent_lessons(cfg, now=time.time() - 45)
    test_eq(got[0]['evidence'], 'mail [EMAIL_1] said so')
    md = lessons_md(got + [dict(lesson='keep notes short', component='rule')])

A replay refuses every shell command, because nobody is there to approve it, but the command a run asked for still shows what it meant to do. refused_commands lists those commands, and judge_prompt puts them under that run’s answer, so the judge can count a needed command, written out for the person to run, as done. ran_commands lists what the person’s own session ran, what failed and what the person declined, with the reason. judge_prompt shows these as what the work needed, and the editor reads the same session as original.md.

        [('git add notes.md && rm draft.md', 'ran', '(no output)'), ('pytest -q', 'failed', 'ERROR: exit 1'), ('git push', 'declined: not yet', '')])
proposer = tn(look, asked, reply='Run `git add notes.md && rm draft.md`; I could not.')
avoider = tn(look, reply='Done.')
p, label = judge_prompt('tidy the drafts', proposer, [avoider], original=tn(ran))
other = 'B' if label == 'A' else 'A'
blocks = {l: p.split(f'## Answer {l}\n')[1].split('\n## ')[0] for l in 'AB'}
assert 'rm draft.md' in blocks[label] and 'rm draft.md' not in blocks[other], blocks   # under the run that asked for it

title: improve
text:
A round
improve_round takes a request and the start record Ramabana wrote for its session, <cfg>/runs/<session>/start.json, which holds repo, head and dirty. It raises ValueError before any run starts when:

the start had uncommitted changes, which a replay from head would not see,
the learned folder holds files outside the allowed layout,
approve is anything but ask or edits, so a replay never runs a shell command,
k is less than 1.

work must be a new folder, or the round raises FileExistsError. Every run, the evidence, the candidate and report.json stay in it. If a base run’s model never answered, the round ends with base_error before the editor runs. If the editor or the candidate run records no turn or gives no answer, the round ends with that error in the report. By default replays refuse every write. approve='edits' lets them edit files inside their own clone, which shares no object files with the source repository. With learned set, a kept lesson goes into the day’s dhrona-<date>.md on a pending/ branch there, and the report names the branch as pending; without it, the round only reports. A lesson that would take the dated files past DATED_MAX characters is not kept, and the report lists that in problems. lessons, rows from recent_lessons, go to the editor as lessons.md.
The tests below use a stand-in script for ramabana that answers each kind of prompt with a fixed reply. Under it, a run takes one call once AGENTS.md exists and three calls before.


source

improve_round
def improve_round(
    prompt, # the request to replay
    start, # `{repo, head, dirty}` from the session's `start.json`
    work, # a new folder for this round's runs, evidence and report
    learned:NoneType=None, # the learned folder whose HEAD the round starts from, and whose `pending/` branch a kept lesson goes onto
    model:NoneType=None, # the model the runs use
    editor:NoneType=None, # the model that edits the candidate
    k:int=2, # base runs
    approve:str='ask', # `edits` lets a replay edit files inside its throwaway clone
    exe:str='ramabana',
    read_outside:bool=True, # replays read outside their clone, as a session started with `--read-outside` does
    original:NoneType=None, # the person's own turn for this request; the editor and the judge see what its commands did
    lessons:tuple=(), # `recent_lessons` rows the editor reads as evidence
    timeout:int=1800, # seconds before a replay, base or candidate, is abandoned
    limit:int=8, # dollars the round's recorded runs may cost before it stops
):
Run one round of k base runs, one edit to the learned folder, one run under the edit and the decision, and return the report.




source

round_cost
def round_cost(
    work
):
Dollars the runs in round folder work recorded, whether or not the round finished; a run that recorded no turn adds nothing.



FAKE = r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"A stand-in for `ramabana`: the editor writes AGENTS.md; a run takes one call once AGENTS.md exists, three before."
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path

title: improve
text:
Training on past sessions
Older sessions have no start.json, so they record no starting commit, and most record no folder either. session_start works both out. It places a turn in the repository that most of its absolute tool paths fall in, or else the first git repository among roots. Its head is that repository’s last commit before the turn’s at, which may be epoch seconds or an ISO date; an unreadable at leaves the turn unplaced. dirty is None because nobody knows what was uncommitted at that time.
trainable picks the turns worth replaying. It takes the first turn of each session when the request is at least 40 characters long, carried no attachments, ended complete and without an error, made between 1 and max_calls calls, and cost something, meaning at least one finding or failed call. An attached file belonged only to that session, so a replay could not see it. It also drops a turn that made a commit, because at marks the end of the turn and the commit found for its start would already contain that commit. A request asked in several sessions is kept once, from the cheapest, and the result is ordered by number of calls, fewest first. trainable_sessions runs trainable over Ramabana’s own history and session index, takes each session’s start from its start.json entry for the repository the work used, and drops a session whose entry had uncommitted changes. The entry is matched on the resolved path, because Ramabana writes resolved paths and a tool call may name a path through a link. An unreadable start.json or session index, such as one a crash cut short, counts as missing.

title: improve
text:
Batches
improve_batch runs improve_round on up to n sessions in turn, in the order trainable_sessions gives. Every round starts from the learned folder’s HEAD, so uncommitted text of a person’s never reaches a replay. Each kept lesson waits on its own pending/ branch, so each can be accepted or rejected alone. With cfg set, the batch first expires what went days days unused (expire_learned, listed in expired.json) and gives every round the lessons of the last days days (recent_lessons). With compact_at set, it then proposes a compaction of AGENTS.md when the file is over that fraction of LEARNED_MAX (see Compaction), and writes the result to compaction.json. models keeps the sessions recorded with those models, and skip leaves sessions out by id. A round that fails, for example because its model cannot start or its repository is gone, becomes a row with error, and the batch goes on. summary.json in work holds every row so far, and [] when no session matched. An approve other than ask or edits raises before any round runs. Uncommitted files in the learned folder never stop a batch.
Each row has a cost: the dollars recorded by every run in the round’s folder (round_cost), meaning the base runs, the editor, the candidate and the judge, whether or not the round finished. A run killed at its timeout, or one whose model reports no cost, adds nothing. With budget set, no new round starts once the rounds so far have cost that much, so a batch can overshoot its budget by the cost of its last round. A batch with a learned folder holds learned_lock on it for its whole run, and a second batch on the same folder, from the command line or a scheduled beat, raises RuntimeError before it creates anything. The lock is a file beside the folder, and the operating system releases it when the batch’s process ends, even in a crash. dhrona-improve runs a batch from the command line. It requires a learned folder, and prints one line per round, with the pending branches and REVIEW, which says to review them with /learned in Ramabana or ramabana-learned in a shell.

Remove each committed dated learning file whose date is over days days old, one commit per file as Dhrona; returns the names. Only that file’s path is staged or committed, so other edits stay as they are.


expire_learned removes what Dhrona proposed and a person accepted once it has gone days days without use or renewal, and commits the removal so git revert brings it back. A skill counts as used when a session read it with read_skill or the turn loaded it, and renewed when a later accepted round changed it. AGENTS.md is in every briefing, so a paragraph there counts only as renewed when an accepted round last changed one of its lines; a fenced block is never split. Only commits whose message starts with LESSON can expire: what was there before Dhrona, and anything a person committed, stays. When nobody worked in the last days days, nothing expires, because nothing had the chance to be used. While the folder has uncommitted changes, skills and AGENTS.md paragraphs do not expire, because the removal is committed with the files it changed and must not stage a person’s edit. It stages and commits only the paths it changed.
expire_dated removes each committed dated learning file over DATED_DAYS (30) days old, by the date in its name. It runs git rm and a commit on that one path as Dhrona, one commit a file, and touches no other path. It works on a folder with uncommitted edits. expire_learned calls it first, so a dated file expires even when nobody worked.

Compaction
Accepted lessons add up, and ramabana-learned accept refuses one that would take AGENTS.md past LEARNED_MAX. compact_learned proposes a shorter file. git blame splits HEAD’s AGENTS.md into paragraphs Dhrona proposed, where every line came from a commit whose message starts with LESSON or COMPACT, and the rest, which a person wrote or which was there before Dhrona. The editor model rewrites only Dhrona’s paragraphs. It merges lessons that overlap, drops duplicates and lessons a later one replaced, and keeps fenced code blocks whole, aiming at target characters (COMPACT_TARGET, 1,200) for the whole file. A person’s paragraph stands in the file as a marker line such as [kept 1], with its text given separately for context, and the marker becomes the original paragraph again, byte for byte. The prompt and the rewrite are scrubbed.
A rewrite is refused, and nothing is committed, when it drops, moves, repeats or edits a marker, drops a fenced block, is no shorter than the file it started from, or passes LEARNED_MAX. One that passes waits on a pending/ branch like a kept candidate, so a person reviews it with ramabana-learned. Its commit message starts with COMPACT, so what it wrote counts as Dhrona’s own: it expires as a lesson does, and a later compaction may rewrite it. Accepting it does not renew the lessons it rewrote. Each rewritten paragraph takes the newest time of the lessons it draws on, matched by shared words, or of all of them when none matches, and the commit’s TIMES trailer records that time for each of its lines. _blame reads the trailer, so a paragraph merged from two stale lessons expires on their schedule, not 30 days after the accept.
onto folds in a pending candidate that ramabana-learned accept refused for size. The file that candidate would make is compacted, the compaction holds the candidate’s other files too, and its INCLUDES trailer names the candidate, so accepting the compaction accepts the candidate and drops its branch. Ramabana’s accept then moves every other pending candidate onto the new HEAD where it applies cleanly, and marks the rest stale.
compact_learned takes learned_lock. It refuses while a batch runs, when AGENTS.md holds no paragraph Dhrona proposed, and when a compaction is already pending. Uncommitted changes in the folder do not stop it: it works from HEAD and leaves the working tree alone. It returns {ok, pending, before, after, cost}, where before and after are character counts and cost the editor’s dollars, or {ok: False, error}. The editor runs as the judge does: one headless Ramabana turn with the editor model, in an empty folder. A test passes chat, a function from prompt to reply.

text:
History health
Ramabana’s history is a log nobody reads until it is 224 MB. history_health makes one streaming pass over it, one line at a time, and reports its size, the rows and bytes of each day, the largest row, and the groups of failing tool calls. A group is a tool plus the first 60 characters of an ERROR result, or of a TypeError about a missing positional argument, counted over the last days and over the days before. A defect is a tool that crashed, a habit is the model or the guard disagreeing about how to use a tool, and noise is a shell command that exited non-zero.

history_health
def history_health(
    cfg:str='~/.config/ramabana', # Ramabana's config folder, whose `agent-history.jsonl` is read
    days:int=14, # the window; the `days` before it give each group's `previous` count
    now:NoneType=None, # epoch seconds; the present when None
    top:int=20, # groups to return, most frequent first
    fixed:NoneType=None, # `load_fixed` rows: a group's occurrences at or before its fix time are not counted
):
One streaming pass over cfg’s history: log size, rows and bytes per day, the largest row, failing-call groups, guard refusals, repeated calls and sub-agent results without a state: line.


A night’s note gets a line for each threshold the report crosses: a log over LOG_MAX_MB or growing over LOG_GROWTH_MB a day for a week, a row over ROW_MAX_MB, and a defect group seen more than DEFECT_MAX times or twice as often as in the window before. Each such defect also gets an issue draft in the night’s folder, with its count and trend, three example sessions, one raw error and the tool. A habit is never an issue: past DEFECT_MAX it becomes a candidate lesson, which a person reviews before anything is learned.
A defect a person has fixed goes in the fixed-defects record, FIXED (~/.config/dhrona/fixed.json, moved by XDG_CONFIG_HOME), keyed by the slug that names its issue draft. Each entry holds at, when the fix was made, a note such as a commit or a version, and an optional check. record_fix writes an entry, and dhrona-fixed SLUG --note NOTE --check CHECK does the same from a shell. history_health counts only the occurrences after at. A defect with any occurrence after at is reported as recurred after fix, whatever its count, and its issue draft says so. A defect with none is not reported and gets no draft.
A check is a shell command or a module:callable path. A shell command passes on exit 0. A callable passes when it returns without raising and does not return False. A check that runs longer than 60 seconds fails. Before each night’s batch, nightly runs every recorded check once (check_lines) and puts each failure in the note as fix check failed for SLUG.

Efficiency
A round asks whether a lesson makes one answer better. The efficiency check asks what the turns cost. A turn’s cost grows with its tool calls, because each call sends the whole context to the model again. efficiency_of reads history rows and counts, per turn: tool calls, input tokens, and the habits that add calls without adding work. efficiency_findings gives a night’s note one line for each threshold that the counts cross.

shell output written to /tmp files and read back


sleeps
shell calls that sleep to wait for background work


test_reruns
the same test command run again with no edit between


memory_writes, memory_reads
notes written much more often than they are read



A habit is reported when it occurs more than EFF_HABIT times in the last EFF_DAYS days. efficiency reads those days from Ramabana’s history.

Every night
nightly is the function a scheduled beat calls. ramabana-tick finds it through the ramabana.ticks entry point named dhrona, and calls it when the pobblebonk schedule named dhrona fires, passing the schedule’s payload as fire. The payload must hold a positive budget in dollars, or nightly raises ValueError before any round runs. A timeout that is not a positive number, given as a number or as text, raises the same way. The other keys are optional:








key
meaning
default




n
rounds
3


k
base runs per round
2


model
the model the replays use
each session’s own


editor
the model that edits and judges
Ramabana’s default


models
a list of model ids whose sessions are kept
all


max_calls
the most calls a replayed turn may have made
40


cfg
the Ramabana config folder
~/.config/ramabana


learned
the learned folder
<cfg>/learned, the folder Ramabana loads

where batch folders go
NIGHTLY, ~/.cache/dhrona/nightly

days of history the lessons come from, and that a proposed skill or rule may go unused before it expires
30


compact_at
the fraction of LEARNED_MAX past which AGENTS.md gets a compaction proposed
0.8


timeout
seconds before a replay, base or candidate, is abandoned; its batch row then carries the run in ... was still going after Ns
1800


exe
the Ramabana command
see below


fixed
the fixed-defects record (see History health)
FIXED, ~/.config/dhrona/fixed.json



Each night writes a new batch folder under work, named by the time it started. It skips every session that a batch under work has already started a round on (tried_sessions), including rounds that failed, and when no session is left it creates nothing. A night with no session left still expires what went unused. nightly returns the note the beat leaves for the next session: how many rounds ran, the pending branches waiting for review, what expired, each recorded fix check that failed, a compaction it proposed, and the dollars spent against the budget.
After expiry and before the rounds, a night proposes a compaction when AGENTS.md is over compact_at of LEARNED_MAX, holds a paragraph Dhrona proposed, and has no compaction pending. The note says compaction pending <branch>, or why none was proposed. A night tries one compaction per HEAD: the HEAD it tried is kept in a file beside the learned folder, so a compaction a person rejected is not proposed again until HEAD moves. The editor’s turn counts against budget: its cost is in the night’s total, in the note’s compaction line and in compaction.json, and a compaction that spends the budget leaves no round to run.
The note names each failed round with the first line of its error (night_error). Where Ramabana’s error suggests /model NAME, which only an interactive session can act on, the note names the schedule key to set instead: model when the replay’s own model could not run, editor otherwise. An error saying Claude Code is not logged in, as happens when a job started by launchd cannot read the login from the keychain, gets a line saying to run claude /login or to put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in Ramabana’s beat.env, which bills the API instead of the subscription.
A night where every round failed and nothing was spent could not run at all: a missing tool, a model that does not start, a lost login. It writes the note into a night-failed file in its batch folder and raises NightFailed with the note as its message, so pobblebonk retries the fire and, after the last try, leaves the note as gave up after N tries. tried_sessions does not count a session from such a night until it has sat in FAILED_TRIES (2) of them, so the retry replays the same sessions and a session that never runs is eventually passed over. A night with no session left, or with one round that ran, returns its note and is not retried.
If a batch is already running on the learned folder, the night returns a note saying so and runs nothing. pobblebonk 0.0.4 and later renew a running fire’s claim, so this only happens when a second beat starts while one is still running. Any other failure raises, and pobblebonk retries a fire that raised, up to the schedule’s retries. Add the schedule with retries=2 and retry_after='1h', so a night that could not run gets one more try an hour later (pobblebonk 0.0.5; an older pobblebonk retries after 30 seconds instead):
from ramabana.monitor import pob
pob().add('dhrona', cron='0 3 * * *', retries=2, retry_after='1h', budget=20, n=3)
An existing schedule takes the same change with pob().update('dhrona', retries=2, retry_after='1h'). Each try runs replays under timeout, and the beat that runs them stops itself after ramabana-tick --limit, so a night cannot hold the beat forever.
Without exe, a night runs the ramabana installed beside the Python that runs the beat, or else the one found on PATH. This matters because a beat started by cron or launchd has a short PATH.

text:
Read Ramabana history
Ramabana appends each finished turn to ~/.config/ramabana/agent-history.jsonl, one JSON object per line. A turn holds the prompt, the reply, the session it belongs to, and an activity list with one row per tool call: the tool’s name, its arguments, the result in detail, and ok for whether it succeeded. A result longer than 600 characters is kept whole in <cfg>/<log>-details/<session>.jsonl, and the row keeps its start and a details reference. read_history reads the file and puts those results back whole through Ramabana’s hydrate_turns, so a row written before Ramabana 0.2.59 reads as it always did, and tool_args returns a call’s arguments as a dict even when the row stored them as JSON text.


source

tool_args
def tool_args(
    action
):
The call arguments of action as a dict.




source

read_history
def read_history(
    path:pathlib.PosixPath=Path('/home/runner/.config/ramabana/agent-history.jsonl'), # Ramabana `agent-history.jsonl` path
    session:NoneType=None, # optional session id
):
Read finished Ramabana turns in the order they were written, skipping incomplete lines, with long tool results whole.



# synthetic logs only: a long result comes back whole from its details file, an old inline row is unchanged,
# and a missing details file or a reference out of the config folder leaves the clipped text
import tempfile
from fastcore.test import test_eq

        {'session': 'a', 'prompt': 'new', 'details': 'agent-details/a.jsonl', 'activity': [{'id': 'c1', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': long[:600]}]},
        {'session': 'b', 'prompt': 'gone', 'details': 'agent-details/b.jsonl', 'activity': [{'id': 'c2', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': 'y' * 600}]},
        {'session': 'b', 'prompt': 'out', 'details': '../x/a.jsonl', 'activity': [{'id': 'c1', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': 'z'}]}]

(d/'agent-details').mkdir(); (d/'agent-details'/'a.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps({'turn_id': '', 'details': {'c1': long}}) + '\n')
got = read_history(d/'agent-history.jsonl')
assert isinstance(got, L)
test_eq([t['activity'][0]['detail'] for t in got], ['inline', long, 'y' * 600, 'z'])
test_eq(read_history(d/'agent-history.jsonl', session='a').attrgot('prompt'), ['old', 'new'])
# the inline log keeps its own details folder beside it
(d/'inline-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(rows[1] | {'details': 'inline-details/a.jsonl'}) + '\n')

text:
Assess a route
A route is the sequence of tool calls a turn made. assess_turn checks it for six kinds of problem and returns an Assessment: a score that starts at 100 and loses 20 points per Finding, the number of calls, and the findings themselves. A route is marked down when:

the request names GitHub and FOSSICK but the first research call is something other than fossick read-gh-repo (route),
a tool could not decode the arguments it was sent (schema),
a shell command does what a dedicated tool does (bypass),
a shell command fails with a usage error (tool_protocol); a test that really fails is not one,
a call that already failed is repeated with the same arguments (repeat_failure),
a call the person refused is made again instead of asking them (denial_retry).

assess_history assesses several turns together, and each of its findings records the turn it came from.


source

assess_history
def assess_history(
    turns
):
Assess several turns as one route corpus, carrying refusals into the next turn of the same session.




source

assess_turn
def assess_turn(
    turn, denied:tuple=()
):
Score the tool calls of one Ramabana turn, where denied holds calls refused in the previous turn.




source

denial_reason
def denial_reason(
    action
):
The reason given for a refused approval, or None when action is not a refusal.




source

bypass_tool
def bypass_tool(
    command, offered:NoneType=None
):
The dedicated tool that command stands in for, or None when some part of it needs the shell.


This turn was asked to use FOSSICK on a GitHub repository but began with a web search, so it loses 20 points for its route.

bad_route = {
    'prompt': 'Use fossick to research https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo',
    'activity': [
        {'tool': 'web_search', 'ok': True, 'args': {'query': 'llmdojo'}},
        {'tool': 'run_shell', 'ok': True,
         'args': {'command': 'fossick read-gh-repo https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo'}},
    ],
}
a = assess_turn(bad_route)
assert a.score == 80 and a.findings[0].kind == 'route'
a

A malformed edit sent twice earns a schema finding each time, and the second call also earns a repeat_failure, because the model did not change course after the first failure.

bad_edit = {'activity': [
    {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'ok': False, 'args': {'commands': ''},
     'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'},
    {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'ok': False, 'args': {'commands': ''},
     'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'},
]}
a = assess_turn(bad_edit)
assert [f.kind for f in a.findings] == ['schema', 'repeat_failure', 'schema']
a


json_error = {'activity': [{'tool': 'edit_cell', 'ok': False, 'args': {'commands': ''}, 'detail': 'ERROR: JSONDecodeError while parsing commands'}]}
assert assess_turn(json_error).findings[0].kind == 'schema'

bypass_tool names the dedicated tool a shell command stands in for, or returns None. It splits the command at &&, ||, ; and newlines, ignoring those inside quotes and heredoc bodies, and looks at the part of each piece before any |. Every piece must map to a tool, because a piece with no tool needed the shell anyway, and the answer is the first piece’s tool. cd pieces, env and VAR=value prefixes, and git’s global options (-C, -c, --no-pager) are ignored. A command that ends in & maps to the background runner, run_shell_bg. When offered is given, a tool outside it gives None.

assert bypass_tool('git diff --stat') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('cd /x && git status --short') == 'git_status'
assert bypass_tool('env A=1 rg foo src') == 'grep'
assert bypass_tool('git show HEAD~1') is None   # git_log lists commits; no tool shows a commit's contents
assert bypass_tool('git log -p -3') is None and bypass_tool('git log --stat -5') is None and bypass_tool('git log -S foo') is None
assert not any(bypass_tool(f'git log {o}') for o in ('-Sfoo', '-Gfoo', '--shortstat', '-u', '--patch-with-stat', '-L1,5:a.py'))
assert bypass_tool('git log --oneline -3') == 'git_log'
assert bypass_tool('git push origin main') == 'git_remote'
assert bypass_tool("sed -n '1,80p' pyproject.toml") == 'view_file'
assert bypass_tool("sed -i 's/a/b/' f.py") == 'replace_text'
assert bypass_tool("cat > f.py <<'PY'") == 'create_file'
assert bypass_tool('cat README.md') == 'view_file'
assert bypass_tool('curl -s https://x.y') == 'read_url'
assert bypass_tool('kosha daemon &') == 'run_shell_bg'
assert bypass_tool('uv run pytest -q | tail -5') is None
assert bypass_tool('git blame f.py') is None
assert bypass_tool('git diff', offered={'run_shell'}) is None
assert tool_args({'args': '{"command": "ls"}'}) == {'command': 'ls'}
assert tool_args({'args': 'not json'}) == {} and tool_args({}) == {}
assert bypass_tool('FOO=1 BAR=2 git status') == 'git_status'
assert bypass_tool('git -C /x diff') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('git --no-pager log -3') == 'git_log'
assert bypass_tool('git -c core.pager=cat -C /x log -3') == 'git_log'
assert bypass_tool(None) is None and bypass_tool('') is None
assert bypass_tool('git diff --stat HEAD main') is None and bypass_tool('git diff HEAD~1') is None   # git_diff shows the working tree or index, not refs
assert bypass_tool('git diff --staged -- a.py') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('git add x.py && git status --short') is None   # the shell was needed for `git add` anyway
assert bypass_tool('git status && git diff') == 'git_status'
assert (bypass_tool('rg "a; b" src'), bypass_tool('git commit -m "fix; tidy"'), bypass_tool('sed -n "1,5p;9,12p" f.py')) == ('grep', 'git_commit', 'view_file')   # separators inside quotes
assert bypass_tool("cat > f.py <<'PY'\nx = 1; y = 2\nPY") == 'create_file'   # a heredoc body is not a command
assert bypass_tool('git diff 2>&1') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('rg "a \\" && b" src') == 'grep'   # an escaped quote stays inside the string
assert bypass_tool('git status\nrm -rf build') is None and bypass_tool('ls\necho $((1<<3))') is None   # a newline separates commands; `<<3` is no heredoc
assert bypass_tool('cat > f.txt <<EOF\nhi; there\nEOF\nrm -rf build') is None   # the command after a heredoc still counts
assert bypass_tool('cat <<EOF > f.txt\nx\nEOF') == 'create_file'

A schema finding applies to any tool whose arguments failed to decode. A bypass finding applies only to run_shell.

t = {'prompt': 'x', 'activity': [
    {'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': 'git diff'}, 'ok': True},
    {'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': 'x'}, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSONDecodeError: Extra data'},
    {'tool': 'replace_text', 'args': '{}', 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSON decoder failed'},
    {'ok': False}]}
kinds = [(f.kind, f.tool) for f in assess_turn(t).findings]
assert ('bypass', 'run_shell') in kinds and ('schema', 'run_shell') in kinds and ('schema', 'replace_text') in kinds
assert ('tool_protocol', 'run_shell') not in kinds  # precedence bug regression

A turn gets one bypass finding per dedicated tool, however many shell calls stood in for it. A row with no ok key is treated as unknown, not as a failure.

t = {'activity': [{'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': c}, 'ok': True} for c in ('git diff', 'git diff --stat', 'git diff HEAD~1', 'cat f')]}
assert [f.kind for f in assess_turn(t).findings] == ['bypass', 'bypass']
unknown = {'activity': [{'tool': 'edit_cell', 'args': {}, 'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'}]*2}
assert assess_turn(unknown).findings == ()

Some calls need a person’s approval. A refusal is recorded as a failed row of kind ask, or as a failed row whose detail starts with Denied by human operator. denial_reason returns the reason the person gave, 'no reason given' when there is none, and None for a row that is not a refusal. A refusal on its own is not a tool failure and earns no finding. Making the same call again instead of asking the person is a denial_retry, whether it happens later in the same turn or in the next turn of the same session when the reply in between asked no question.

edit = {'tool': 'replace_text', 'args': {'path': 'x.py', 'edits': []}}
refused = {**edit, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator. Reason given: no answer after 300s'}
assert denial_reason(refused) == 'no answer after 300s'
assert denial_reason({**edit, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}) == 'no reason given'
assert denial_reason({**edit, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSONDecodeError'}) is None and denial_reason({**edit, 'ok': True}) is None
assert assess_turn({'activity': [refused]}).findings == ()
assert [f.kind for f in assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}]}).findings] == ['denial_retry']
a = assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': True}]})
assert [(f.kind, f.tool, f.index) for f in a.findings] == [('denial_retry', 'replace_text', 1)] and a.score == 80
assert a.findings[0].message == 'Ask the user about the refused call instead of retrying it.'
a = assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}, {**edit, 'ok': True}]})
assert [f.kind for f in a.findings] == ['denial_retry', 'denial_retry']
assert assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'args': {'path': 'y.py', 'edits': []}, 'ok': True}]}).findings == ()
assert assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'args': {}, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'}]}).findings[0].kind == 'schema'


stall = {'session': 's1', 'reply': 'I will retry the edit.', 'activity': [refused]}
retry = {'session': 's1', 'reply': 'Done.', 'activity': [{**edit, 'ok': True}]}
asked = {**stall, 'reply': 'The edit needs your approval. Shall I apply it?'}
assert [f.kind for f in assess_history([stall, retry]).findings] == ['denial_retry']
assert assess_history([stall, retry]).findings[0].index == 0
assert assess_history([asked, retry]).findings == ()
assert assess_history([stall, {**retry, 'session': 's2'}]).findings == ()
assert assess_history([stall, {'session': 's1', 'reply': 'x', 'activity': []}, retry]).findings == ()
assert assess_history([stall, {**retry, 'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': True}]}]).findings[0].index == 0

assert Finding('a', 'b', 0, 'm').turn is None and asdict(Finding('a', 'b', 0, 'm', turn=2))['turn'] == 2   # positional construction still works
assert [f.turn for f in assess_history([stall, retry]).findings] == [1] and [f.turn for f in assess_turn(retry, {_failure_key(refused)}).findings] == [None]
assert [f.turn for f in assess_history([bad_route, stall, retry]).findings] == [0, 2]

A history file may end in a line the agent has not finished writing. read_history skips it, and blank lines too.

from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'h.jsonl'
    p.write_text('{"session": "a"}\n\n{"session": "b"}\n{"sess')
    assert read_history(p).attrgot('session') == ['a', 'b']

text:
Build the warm start
A warm start is chat history made from accepted rounds, placed in front of a new chat so the model sees good tool use first. warm_start builds it in Urai’s message format from the user’s library in ROUNDS_DIR and the seeds packaged with dhrona in SEEDS_DIR. When you pass the tools you offer, a round is replayed only if every recorded call still binds to the offered tool’s signature. Rounds are sorted by meta.rank, lower first and 50 when it is missing, and then rounds recorded on model come first. The sort is stable, so a library round comes before a seed of equal rank. limit keeps the first few, 2 by default. Rishi re-exports the same chat format, so any Rishi backend can continue this history through messages=, and prepare_chat puts the warm start into an empty chat object.

hist = warm_start()
assert [tc.name for m in hist if m.get('tool_calls') for tc in m['tool_calls']] == ['git_status', 'git_diff', 'git_commit', 'git_divergence', 'git_remote', 'search_code', 'grep', 'ls']
assert hist[2]['tool_call_id'] == hist[1]['tool_calls'][0]['id']
hist[:3]

call_valid checks one call by binding its arguments to the tool’s signature. inspect.signature follows functools.wraps and accepts any keyword for a **kwargs parameter, so wrapped and permissive tools pass. round_valid checks every call in a round, and misfit says why a round does not fit.

import functools
def run_shell(command, cwd='.', timeout=60): ...
def grep(pattern, **kw): ...
@functools.wraps(run_shell)
def wrapped(*a, **k): return run_shell(*a, **k)
assert call_valid({'command': 'ls'}, run_shell) and not call_valid({}, run_shell)
assert not call_valid({'command': 'ls', 'bogus': 1}, run_shell)
assert call_valid({'pattern': 'x', 'anything': 1}, grep) and call_valid({'command': 'ls'}, wrapped)

seed = next(r for r in load_rounds([SEEDS_DIR]) if r['meta']['name'] == 'fossick-github')
assert round_calls(seed)[0][0] == 'run_shell'
assert round_valid(seed, as_tools([run_shell])) and not round_valid(seed, as_tools([grep]))
msgs = warm_start([run_shell], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR])
assert msgs[0]['role'] == 'user' and any(m.get('tool_calls') for m in msgs)
assert warm_start([grep], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR]) == []

A missing library folder or an unreadable round file never raises, and warm_start returns what it could read. With no tools given, every round is replayed without checking.

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (Path(d)/'bad.json').write_text('{nope')
    assert warm_start([run_shell], dirs=[Path(d)/'missing', Path(d), SEEDS_DIR]) == msgs
ranked = sorted(load_rounds([SEEDS_DIR]), key=lambda r: r['meta'].get('rank', 50))
assert warm_start(dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=len(ranked)) == [m for r in ranked for m in round_msgs(r)]  # no tools offered: every seed, by rank

The offered tools are read once, so an iterator of callables still checks every round. A tool result with no id is still paired with its call.

import shutil
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    shutil.copy(SEEDS_DIR/'fossick-github.json', Path(d)/'copy.json')
    assert warm_start(iter([run_shell]), dirs=[d, SEEDS_DIR]) == msgs + msgs
noid = {'history': [

The approval-refused seed shows the right response to a refused write: the assistant names the refused action and asks one question instead of trying again. Its calls bind to shalya’s view_file(path, start, end) and replace_text(path, edits), so it is replayed only when those tools are offered. The other seeds each teach one route on the shalya 0.1.0 and ramabana 0.2.0 tool set. git-flow uses the git tools, and its commit result carries an undo token. search-choice picks between semantic search, literal search and a listing. notebook-edit edits notebook cells by id. memory-key shows that a note saved under an existing key replaces the old one, and delegation confirms a sub-agent’s report by reading the lines it cites. Every seed has a rank, so a small limit still picks the most useful lessons.

title: rounds
dhrona
text:
Dhrona studies how a coding agent uses its tools and helps it use them better. It was built for Ramabana, a coding agent that writes every finished turn to a history file: the request, each tool call with its arguments and result, and the reply. Dhrona reads that file.
The sequence of tool calls an agent makes to answer one request is its route. Some routes are poor. The agent runs git diff through the shell when it has a git_diff tool, sends arguments that do not fit a tool’s signature, or repeats a call that has just failed. Dhrona finds these mistakes and scores each route. It can then teach the agent in two ways. You can keep good sessions as examples, called rounds, and put them in front of a new chat so the model sees good tool use before the first request. Or Dhrona can replay past requests and edit the agent’s learned folder, the notes and skills Ramabana loads into every session, keeping an edit only when the replay goes better.
A few other names appear on these pages. Leela is the notebook editor in which you review a round. Aidialog is the notebook format a round is saved in. Urai is the chat library whose message format a warm start is written in, and Rishi re-exports the same format.

title: dhrona
text:
How the pieces fit

Measure. dhrona-tools counts calls, failures and shell bypasses for each tool and each model. dhrona scores the routes in a history.
Capture. dhrona-capture saves a finished Ramabana session as a review notebook.
Review. Open the notebook in Leela, delete the detours and anything private, and keep the route you want future models to copy.
Accept. dhrona-accept --install records who reviewed the round, which tools it calls and which model ran it, writes the round as JSON and copies it into the rounds library.
Warm start. warm_start(tools, model) turns accepted rounds into the opening history of a new chat. It leaves out any round whose calls no longer fit the tools you offer.

Run dhrona-tools again after a change to see whether tool use moved.

title: dhrona
text:
Measure tool use
dhrona-tools reads the Ramabana and Leela history files and reports, for each tool, how often it was called, how often it failed and how often a person refused it. It also counts the shell commands that did the job of a dedicated tool, and repeats the counts for each model. Save its JSON before you change a tool set and compare it with a later run.
dhrona-tools --since 2026-09-19
dhrona-tools --json > baselines/tools.json
assess_turn scores one turn by its tool calls alone. It does not read the assistant’s text to judge the quality of the work. This turn was asked to use FOSSICK on a GitHub repository but began with a web search:

turn = {
    'prompt': 'Use fossick to research https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo',
    'activity': [{'tool': 'web_search', 'ok': True, 'args': {'query': 'llmdojo'}}],
}
assessment = assess_turn(turn)
assessment

Each problem is a Finding, and its kind says what went wrong:







kind
what happened




route
the request named GitHub and FOSSICK, but the first research call was not fossick read-gh-repo


schema
the tool could not decode the arguments the model sent


bypass
a shell command did the job of a dedicated tool, such as git diff for git_diff


tool_protocol
a shell command failed with a usage error


repeat_failure
the model repeated, with the same arguments, a call that had already failed


denial_retry
the model repeated a call the person had refused, instead of asking them



The score starts at 100 and loses 20 points per finding, down to 0. Each dedicated tool a turn bypasses counts once, so shelling out for both git diff and cat costs 40 points. Run dhrona to assess the default Ramabana history, and pass --session to assess one session.
Some tool calls need a person’s approval. When the person refuses, or nobody answers in time, Ramabana records a failed row of kind ask whose detail starts with Denied by human operator and gives the reason. Dhrona does not treat a refusal as a tool failure, so it earns no schema or repeat_failure finding. dhrona-tools counts refusals separately as denials, with the most common denial_reasons.
The mistake Dhrona does flag is making the refused call again without asking the person, either later in the same turn or in the next turn of the session when the reply in between asked no question. That is a denial_retry. The packaged approval-refused seed shows the better answer: name the refused edit, say that nothing changed, and ask one question.

title: dhrona
text:
Curate a round
A round is one short session kept as an example of the right way to use the tools. You make one from a real session. Ramabana already records each finished turn, so capture reads that record after the conversation ends. It does not watch a running agent.
ramabana --root /path/to/project
# finish the useful conversation, then quit
dhrona-capture training/github-research.ipynb --session latest
leela training
Open github-research.ipynb in Leela. Delete the detours and anything private, and keep the route future models should copy. Save the notebook, then accept it under your name:
dhrona-accept training/github-research.ipynb --reviewer Karthik --install
Accepting writes the reviewer, the tools the round calls and the model that ran it into the notebook’s metadata, and writes github-research.json beside the notebook with the round’s messages. --install also copies that file into the rounds library, ~/.config/dhrona/rounds/, where warm_start looks for rounds. A notebook that has not been accepted cannot start a session.
dhrona-start prints the two Ramabana commands that start a session from an accepted round: one sends the round as the first turn, and the other resumes that session. --launch runs them.
dhrona-start training/github-research.ipynb --root /path/to/project
dhrona-start training/github-research.ipynb --root /path/to/project --launch
Ramabana has no option for loading prepared history, so the first command sends the whole round as one prompt that ends by asking for the reply DHRONA_READY. Ramabana saves that turn, and the second command resumes the session for real work. Leela can read the same history directly with compiled_history once it supports prepared history.

title: dhrona
text:
Warm start a chat
A warm start puts a few accepted rounds at the front of a new chat’s history, so the model sees good tool use before the first real request. warm_start builds that history in Urai’s message format from two places: your rounds library and the seeds packaged with dhrona.
Pass the tools you will offer, as a list of callables or names, or as a dict from name to callable. A round is used only if each of its recorded calls still binds to the offered tool’s signature (call_valid), so a round for a tool that has since been renamed or changed is left out rather than taught. Rounds are ordered by meta.rank, lower first, then by whether they were recorded on the same model, and limit (2 by default) keeps the first few. Pass the result to any Urai or Rishi chat as messages=, or call prepare_chat on an empty chat.

title: dhrona
text:
Improve the learned folder
Ramabana loads a learned folder into every session: an AGENTS.md of short rules, and skills it opens when a task needs them. improve_round tries to improve that folder from one finished session, following the propose, probe and compose step of Harness². It replays the session’s request from the commit the session started at, k times under the current folder. An editor model reads those runs and edits a copy of the folder, and the request is replayed once more under the copy. The copy is kept only when that run replied, took a cheaper route than every earlier run, and a judge model rated its reply at least as good as the best of theirs. A route’s cost is its findings, then its failed calls, then its number of calls, and refused approvals do not count. A kept lesson becomes a short entry in the day’s learning file, dhrona-<date>.md, committed on a pending/ branch of the learned folder’s own git repository. Ramabana reads only what a person accepted, with ramabana-learned accept. Uncommitted files in the folder never stop a batch, and Dhrona never stages, commits or discards them. Replays start from the folder’s committed HEAD. Dated files hold at most 4,000 characters together, and one older than 30 days is removed at the next batch. The editor also reads the lessons the agent recorded with remember, and a lesson about a broken tool can become a skill that works around it. Emails, phone numbers, keys and other personal details are scrubbed with rahasya before the editor or the judge sees anything, and before anything is kept. A skill or rule Dhrona proposed that goes 30 days without use expires at the next batch. When accepted lessons crowd AGENTS.md, compact_learned asks the editor to merge and shorten the paragraphs Dhrona wrote, leaves every paragraph a person wrote as it was, and proposes the result on a pending/ branch for review like any lesson. A night does the same once AGENTS.md passes 80% of its 2,000 characters.
Ramabana writes the commit a session started at to <cfg>/runs/<session>/start.json. A session that began with uncommitted changes is refused, because a replay from that commit would not see them. A session resumed without that file writes none, and Dhrona then infers its start from the history.
from dhrona.improve import improve_round
start = json.loads(Path('~/.config/ramabana/runs/agent_.../start.json').expanduser().read_text())[0]
report = improve_round(prompt, start, '/tmp/round-1', learned=Path('~/.config/ramabana/learned').expanduser(),
                       model='claude/haiku', editor='claude/sonnet')
Every run, the evidence the editor read, the candidate folder and report.json stay in the work folder, so you can read the candidate’s reply and the judge’s verdict before relying on a kept round.
dhrona-improve runs rounds on past sessions one after another. It picks first turns that make sense on their own and whose route cost something, finds the repository their tool paths touched, and replays each from that repository’s last commit before the turn. Each round starts from the folder the previous round left. summary.json in the batch folder holds one row per round, and a round that fails becomes a row with its error. nightly runs the same kind of batch from a scheduled beat, within a budget in dollars. When a defect the night reports has been fixed, dhrona-fixed SLUG --note NOTE --check CHECK records the fix: later nights count only the failures after it, report a recurrence as recurred after fix, and run CHECK, a shell command or a module:callable path, once before the batch, listing a failure in the night’s note.
dhrona-improve /tmp/batch-1 /tmp/learned --n 10 --editor claude/sonnet --models claude-opus-5-5,claude/sonnet

title: dhrona
text:
Move sessions between hosts
A host is a program that runs agent sessions: Ramabana, Claude Code or Codex. A session from any of the three can be imported as an Aidialog notebook and reviewed in Leela.
dhrona-import ramabana training/round.ipynb --session latest
dhrona-import claude training/round.ipynb --session latest --cwd /path/to/project
dhrona-import codex training/round.ipynb --session latest --cwd /path/to/project
The same reviewed notebook can then be exported as a Ramabana bootstrap prompt, a Claude Code session you can resume, or Codex Responses API items.
dhrona-export training/round.ipynb ramabana --output training/round.txt
dhrona-export training/round.ipynb claude --cwd /path/to/project
dhrona-export training/round.ipynb codex --output training/round-items.json
Claude Code can resume the session id that the Claude export prints. The Codex export cannot make a resumable Codex session, because llmsurgery, the library Dhrona uses to read and write host sessions, has no public writer for Codex rollout files yet. The exported items still serve for inspection and for datasets.

The common dialog
This small dialog shows the part that carries across hosts. One prompt, one tool call, one result and one final reply survive the round trip through an Aidialog notebook and convert to Codex items.

import tempfile
from aidialog.hist import chat2dlg, dlg2chat
from aidialog.msg_parts import Msg, Text, ToolUse, ToolResult

tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
tool = ToolUse(id='call_1', name='search_code', arguments={'query': 'dialog history'})
msgs = [
    Msg('user', [Text('Find the dialog history contract.')]),
    Msg('assistant', [Text('I will inspect the implementation.'), tool]),
    Msg('tool', [ToolResult(id=tool.id, name=tool.name, text='Chat.hist stores canonical messages.')]),
    Msg('assistant', [Text('Urai uses canonical messages in Chat.hist.')]),
]
dlg = chat2dlg(msgs, 'portable', mx=None)
dlg.meta[REVIEW_KEY] = {'status': 'accepted'}
portable = tmp/'portable.ipynb'
_write_dlg(dlg, portable)
roundtrip = dlg2chat(clean_dialog(portable), plain=True)
assert [m.role for m in roundtrip] == ['user', 'assistant', 'tool', 'assistant']
assert roundtrip[1].content[-1].name == 'search_code'
assert roundtrip[2].content[0].text == 'Chat.hist stores canonical messages.'
roundtrip

text: dhrona-tools measures tool use before and after you change an agent’s tool set, for example when you remove tools nobody uses. It reads the Ramabana and Leela history files and reports, for each tool, the calls, failures and refusals. It then lists the shell commands that did a dedicated tool’s job, and gives the same counts for each model.

title: tools
text:
Report
Each turn’s at is a time in seconds since the epoch, so since accepts either that or an ISO date. Older rows may lack tool, ok or args, or hold args as JSON text, and the report accepts all of them. Failures are grouped by the first line of their detail with every number replaced by N, so the same error at different line numbers counts as one. A refused approval, which is an ask row with ok false or a detail starting Denied by human operator, counts as a denial with its reason, not as a failure. fmt_report prints the report as a table.

def tool_report(
    turns, # history turns from `read_history`
    since:NoneType=None, # epoch or ISO date lower bound on `at`
    model:NoneType=None, # restrict to one model name
):
Count calls, failures and denials per tool, shell bypasses, and the same split per model.



AT_OLD, AT_NEW, SINCE_BETWEEN = 1786431016.4, 1790392050.7, 1788000000.0
turns = [
  {'model': 'm1', 'at': AT_OLD, 'activity': [{'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': 'git diff'}, 'ok': True}]},
  {'model': 'm2', 'at': AT_NEW, 'activity': [
     {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'args': '{}', 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSONDecodeError: Extra data at line 3'},
     {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'args': {}, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSONDecodeError: Extra data at line 9'},
     {'tool': 'view_file', 'ok': True}, {'ok': True}]}]
r = tool_report(turns)
assert r['calls'] == 5 and r['tools']['edit_cell']['fails'] == 2 and r['tools']['edit_cell']['fail_rate'] == 1.0
assert r['tools']['edit_cell']['failures'][0][1] == 2
assert r['tools']['edit_cell']['failures'][0][0] == 'JSONDecodeError: Extra data at line N'
assert list(r['tools']) == ['edit_cell', 'run_shell', 'view_file', '?']
assert r['tools']['run_shell']['fails'] == 0 and r['tools']['run_shell']['failures'] == []
assert r['bypass'] == {'git_diff': 1} and r['models']['m1'] == {'calls': 1, 'shell': 1, 'bypass': 1}
assert r['models']['m2'] == {'calls': 4, 'shell': 0, 'bypass': 0}
assert tool_report(turns, since=SINCE_BETWEEN)['calls'] == 4
assert tool_report(turns, since='2026-09-01')['calls'] == 4 and tool_report(turns, since=str(SINCE_BETWEEN))['calls'] == 4
assert tool_report(turns, model='m1')['calls'] == 1
assert tool_report([])['calls'] == 0 and fmt_report(tool_report([]))
assert 'edit_cell' in fmt_report(r) and 'git_diff=1' in fmt_report(r) and 'm1:' in fmt_report(r)
assert dumps(r)
assert tool_report([{'activity': [{'tool': 'x', 'detail': 'boom'}]}])['tools']['x']['fails'] == 0
assert r['denials'] == {} and r['denial_reasons'] == [] and 'denials: none' in fmt_report(r)
refused = [{'tool': 'replace_text', 'args': {'path': 'x.py'}, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator. Reason given: no answer after 300s'},
           {'tool': 'replace_text', 'args': {'path': 'x.py'}, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'Denied by human operator. Reason given: no answer after 900s'},
           {'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': 'rm -rf x'}, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}]
rd = tool_report(turns + [{'model': 'm2', 'at': AT_NEW, 'activity': refused}])
assert rd['denials'] == {'replace_text': 2, 'run_shell': 1}
assert rd['denial_reasons'] == [['no answer after Ns', 2], ['no reason given', 1]]
assert rd['tools']['replace_text'] == {'calls': 2, 'fails': 0, 'fail_rate': 0.0, 'failures': []}
assert rd['calls'] == 8 and rd['models']['m2']['calls'] == 7
assert 'denials: replace_text=2, run_shell=1; no answer after Ns=2, no reason given=1' in fmt_report(rd)

    history:str='', # comma-separated history paths (default: every known history)
    since:str='', # epoch or ISO date lower bound
    model:str='', # restrict to one model
    json:bool=False, # print the report as JSON

Report tool usage, failures and shell bypasses across agent histories.



from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from fastcore.xtras import Path
from json import dumps as _d


with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'h.jsonl'
    p.write_text('\n'.join(_d(t) for t in turns) + '\n{"partial": ')
    assert all(h.exists() for h in HISTORIES)
    tools_cli(history=str(p)); tools_cli(history=str(p), since='2026-09-01', json=True)

A missing history path is named on stderr and skipped. When no file is left, or when --since is neither an epoch nor an ISO date, the command exits with one line instead of a traceback.

import io, contextlib, os
from unittest.mock import patch
from fastcore.test import expect_fail


with expect_fail(ValueError, '--since must be'): _epoch('yesterday')
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p, missing, err = Path(d)/'h.jsonl', f'{d}/missing.jsonl', io.StringIO()
    p.write_text(_d(turns[0]) + '\n')
    with contextlib.redirect_stderr(err): tools_cli(history=f'{p},{missing}')
    assert 'missing.jsonl' in err.getvalue()
    with expect_fail(SystemExit, 'No history'): tools_cli(history=missing)
    with expect_fail(SystemExit, '--since must be'): tools_cli(history=str(p), since='yesterday')
    with patch.dict(os.environ, {'HOME': d}), contextlib.redirect_stdout(out := io.StringIO()): tools_cli(history='~/h.jsonl')
    assert '1 calls' in out.getvalue()
